paragraph: Today's Granville composite lands at a cautious 44 out of 100, capped firmly at 60 due to an active divergence warning where the S&P 500 pushes higher despite a falling RSP-to-SPY breadth ratio of -2.02%. This underlying internal weakness is reinforced by a heavy macro backdrop featuring an elevated VIX at 26.62, a backwardated volatility term structure, and widening high-yield credit spreads currently at 3.76%. Defensive postures are evident through a bullish XLP/XLY rotation of -3.91% and a declining transport-to-S&P ratio of -2.42%, even as aggressive risk appetite shows pockets of life via strong bellwether semi and high-beta signals. Ultimately, the dominant market internals and structural fear metrics dictate a defensive posture for today's session, pointing to a bias toward selling rallies or maintaining cash reserves.
